Class CellBuffer

Namespace
Tuinet
Assembly
Tuinet.dll

A grid of cells plus a cursor position. All writes clip to the buffer and keep wide glyphs consistent: a wide glyph always owns a continuation cell, and overwriting either half blanks the other.

Text writes (Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetString(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Char},Tuinet.Style,System.Int32,Tuinet.Overflow), Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetRune(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Text.Rune,Tuinet.Style)) layer: a default foreground or background in the style keeps the color already in the cell, so text drawn on a filled panel keeps the panel's background. Attributes are replaced. Tuinet.CellBuffer.Fill(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.Style) and Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetCell(System.Int32,System.Int32,Tuinet.Cell) replace whole cells.

Show the terminal cursor at (x, y) after this frame, in shape (e.g. a bar for a text caret). Out-of-range positions hide it. The renderer sends the shape only when it changes, and the terminal's own shape comes back on exit.

SetLink(Rect, ReadOnlySpan<char>)

Make the cells in area a hyperlink to url (OSC 8): terminals that support it open the URL on click (often Ctrl+click), others show the text as is. Draw the text first: text written over a cell later replaces its link, as it does its attributes; Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetStyle(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.Style) keeps it. An empty url removes links. Returns false, removing links instead, for a URL that can't be linked: one with control characters, longer than 2048 chars once encoded, or past the 4095th distinct URL of the process. Spaces and non-ASCII characters are percent-encoded.

int end = buffer.SetString(x, y, "docs", linkStyle);
buffer.SetLink(new Rect(x, y, end - x, 1), "https://example.com/docs");
public bool SetLink(Rect area, ReadOnlySpan<char> url)

SetRune(Rect, Rune, Style)

Fill area with rune (borders, rules, separators). Layers like Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetRune(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Text.Rune,Tuinet.Style): default colors keep the colors already there, attributes are replaced. Zero-width runes draw nothing; wide runes fill pairs of columns.

SetString(int, int, ReadOnlySpan<char>, Style, int, Overflow)

Write text starting at column x, using at most maxWidth columns. Controls and combining marks are dropped. Returns the column after the last glyph written, so styled segments can be chained.

SetText(int, int, StyledText, int, Overflow)

Write styled text, like Tuinet.CellBuffer.SetString(System.Int32,System.Int32,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Char},Tuinet.Style,System.Int32,Tuinet.Overflow) but with a style per run (layered over the text's base style, and over the cells underneath like any text write). Stops at the first glyph that doesn't fit. A run boundary inside a grapheme cluster moves to the cluster's end. With Tuinet.Overflow.Ellipsis, the '…' takes the style of the text it replaces.
